correctness.rationale: Exact uniform arrangement counting gives the mixed falling-factorial expectation E C(U,r)C(K,s)=C(n-m,r)C(m,s)(m)_s/(n)_{r+s}, including r=0,s=0 conventions. Expanding E(1+z)^W from these finite moments gives coefficients relative to exp((mu+nu)z) with mu=(n-m)/n and nu=m²/n. For m in [a sqrt(n), b sqrt(n)] and r+s<=n^{1/8}, the two factors (m)_s/m^s contribute -s(s-1)/m, while other falling factors and second-order errors are O((r+s+1)^4/n). For the complementary high coefficients, factorial majorants plus a superfactorially small r>n/2 tail control the full entire generating polynomial uniformly on fixed complex disks; this justifies summing the local expansion, not merely pointwise moments. Thus F_n(z)=e^{lambda_n z}(1-m³ z²/n²)+O_R(n^-1). Substituting z=w-1 and applying Cauchy on |w|=2 gives an ℓ1 probability remainder O(n^-1), yielding Poisson second differences with sign from (w-1)². At lambda=2, Δ²q(j)=q_2(j)(j-1)(j-4)/4; its ℓ1 norm is 10e^-2/3, giving 5e^-2/3 after TV half-factor. Independent exact-rational factorial inversion for (n,m)=(6,2),(9,3),(16,4) verifies positivity, total mass, mean and signed correction trend, but these finite numbers do not prove uniform analytic error. Only one repeated symbol at m~c sqrt(n) with c in (0,infty) is proved; no result for general multiset profiles.

value.rationale: An existing primary paper explicitly singles out the one-heavy-symbol square-root example because its upper and lower Poisson errors fail to match. This result supplies a nonzero exact leading error and an entire signed ℓ1 asymptotic profile for a natural one-parameter critical family, closing a motivated quantitative gap. It uses a standard approximation framework but performs nonroutine exact mixed-moment summation with a uniform analytic remainder. The result is neither an arbitrary finite computation nor novelty based merely on applying the name Poisson–Charlier.
